overall: The AG found the Medford Zoning Board of Appeals did not violate the Open Meeting Law; crowd accommodation, public comment, and adjournment were upheld, while zoning and September 26 allegations were declined as outside scope or untimely.

allegations.summary: Board failed to accommodate a large crowd at the October 24 hearing, which was initially held in a room too small for the attendance.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we conclude that, by moving the hearing to the largest space available, the Board complied with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Chair limited public comment at the October 24 hearing and refused to open the floor to the public.
allegations.key_passage: The law therefore gives discretion to the chair of the public body to determine who may speak or otherwise participate at a meeting.

allegations.summary: Chair threatened to call police to remove a speaker at the October 24 hearing.
allegations.key_passage: In this instance, the Chair clearly warned Mr. Penta.

allegations.summary: Board prematurely adjourned the October 24 hearing when members of the public stood up to address the Board.
allegations.key_passage: Consequently, we find that the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law by adjourning the hearing when it chose to do so.

allegations.summary: Alleged violation of G.L. c. 40A, section 10 (zoning variances) in the handling of the October 24 hearing.
allegations.key_passage: which is a matter outside the scope of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board scheduled the September 26 hearing at the same time as a Medford City Council meeting, limiting attendance.
allegations.key_passage: Because this complaint was filed with the Board on October 30, we find that this specific allegation is untimely and we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Insufficient notice of the September 26 hearing, including failure to notify nearby neighbors in writing.
allegations.key_passage: Here, any complaint concerning the September 26 hearing should have been filed with the Committee within thirty days of the hearing, or by October 26.
